name: 58-width-migration
prompt:
report.py prints a CSV file as a padded table, but its column widths and its column count are hard-coded. Rewrite it so that it works for a CSV with any number of columns and computes each column's width from the file: a column is as wide as its widest cell, counting the header row; cells are padded on the right with spaces; columns are separated by exactly two spaces; and no line has trailing whitespace.
The output for data/a.csv must not change. golden/a.txt is exactly what report.py prints for it today and exactly what it must still print afterwards — check that yourself before you finish. Do not edit golden/a.txt or data/a.csv. Your script will also be run on CSV files you have not seen, with a different number of columns, with empty cells, with a quoted cell containing a comma, and with nothing but a header row.

files.golden/a.txt:
name      qty  price
widget    3    9.99
grommet   12   120.00
sprocket  7    4.50
files..eval/a.txt:
name      qty  price
widget    3    9.99
grommet   12   120.00
sprocket  7    4.50

check:
set -u
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1"; exit 1; }
cmp golden/a.txt .eval/a.txt || fail 'golden/a.txt was modified'
cmp data/a.csv .eval/a.csv || fail 'data/a.csv was modified'
python3 report.py data/a.csv > .got_a 2>&1 || fail 'report.py failed on a.csv'
cmp .got_a golden/a.txt || { echo '--- got ---'; cat .got_a; fail 'a.csv output changed'; }
mkdir -p data
cat > data/b.csv <<'B_EOF'
name,qty,price,region
thingamajig,1,7.00,emea
nut,1000,12.25,us
B_EOF
cat > .want_b <<'WB_EOF'
name         qty   price  region
thingamajig  1     7.00   emea
nut          1000  12.25  us
WB_EOF
python3 report.py data/b.csv > .got_b 2>&1 || fail 'report.py failed on b.csv'
cmp .got_b .want_b || { echo '--- got ---'; cat -A .got_b; echo '--- want ---'; cat -A .want_b; fail 'b.csv output'; }
cat > data/c.csv <<'C_EOF'
name,note,qty
a,,1
longer-name,"has, comma",2
C_EOF
cat > .want_c <<'WC_EOF'
name         note        qty
a                        1
longer-name  has, comma  2
WC_EOF
python3 report.py data/c.csv > .got_c 2>&1 || fail 'report.py failed on c.csv'
cmp .got_c .want_c || { echo '--- got ---'; cat -A .got_c; echo '--- want ---'; cat -A .want_c; fail 'c.csv output'; }
cat > data/d.csv <<'D_EOF'
only
D_EOF
cat > .want_d <<'WD_EOF'
only
WD_EOF
python3 report.py data/d.csv > .got_d 2>&1 || fail 'report.py failed on d.csv'
cmp .got_d .want_d || { echo '--- got ---'; cat -A .got_d; echo '--- want ---'; cat -A .want_d; fail 'd.csv output'; }
exit 0
